name: Tyrannus
overview: Tyrannus was a male figure known for running a school in Ephesus, as recorded in Acts 19:9. Beyond this unique attribute, Scripture does not provide additional details about his tribe or other personal notes. His role as an educator or leader of a gathering place for teaching is highlighted in the biblical text.
namesAndTitles: The name Tyrannus appears as a proper name in Acts 19:9. No specific meaning or divine origin of the name is indicated in the biblical record. Therefore, the name is simply acknowledged as the identifier of this individual without further semantic significance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships or personal connections for Tyrannus beyond his role in running a school in Ephesus. There are no listed relatives or associates directly linked to him in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Tyrannus holds significance in the New Testament narrative as the individual who provided a venue for teaching in Ephesus, facilitating the spread of the gospel and apostolic instruction. His school served as an important setting for ministry activity during Paul's time in the city. This contribution underscores the practical support given to early Christian teaching and community formation.
